page: Amazon Web Services m5d.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by dual Intel Xeon 8175M processors based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs operating at a 3.1 GHz clock rate. System memory is configured with 384 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Integrated hardware includes 3,600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps. The server operates without a hypervisor layer and does not include GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reflects strong multi-core processing efficiency, ranking in the top tier for multi-threaded stress-ng tasks, software compilation with Clang, and PassMark CPU metrics. Large block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 216.75 GB/sec, supporting database operations and Redis SET throughput exceeding 76 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput also achieves high volume at 48.67 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core metrics in Geekbench and compression tasks operate within median brackets, and lack of discrete acceleration produces low token throughput on large language model generation benchmarks.

Direct access to underlying hardware removes virtualization overhead, enabling full utilization of advanced CPU instruction flags and virtualization hooks. The combination of dense thread counts, balanced memory, and high-capacity NVMe storage delivers strong resource efficiency for I/O-intensive and concurrent computing tasks. The platform is well suited for relational database engines, distributed caching nodes, CI/CD build environments, and container host fleets requiring dedicated hardware execution.
description: Amazon Web Services m5d.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose instance featuring 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs on the Intel Xeon 8175M x86_64 architecture running at 3.1 GHz. The platform is provisioned with 384 GB of DDR4 system memory, 3,600 GB of attached NVMe SSD storage, and 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without GPU accelerators. Benchmark results indicate high multi-threaded performance, robust uncached memory read bandwidth of 216.75 GB/sec, and strong execution throughput in Redis operations and static web serving, while single-threaded tasks perform in the median range. Eliminating hypervisor layers provides full hardware utilization and predictable compute delivery. Due to its balanced vCPU-to-memory allocation and low-latency local storage, m5d.metal is well matched for high-concurrency database deployments, in-memory caching systems, large-scale software compilation, and container virtualization infrastructure.
